scope: Version-aware advanced inference chapter with original diagram and explicit toy/derived claims.

claims.claim: Speculative decoding proposes draft tokens and verifies them with the target model to reduce decode serial work in supported workloads.
The official vLLM guide describes standard speculative rejection sampling as theoretically distribution-preserving up to numerical precision, while FLy deliberately relaxes verification.
Documented common methods include draft_model, ngram, suffix, mtp, eagle3 and dflash with method-specific configuration.
The upstream guide provides n-gram speculation using method=ngram and num_speculative_tokens, with prompt lookup bounds.
Per-request speculative acceptance metrics are documented separately from ordinary output token metrics.
Standard speculative sampling accepts a draft token x with probability min(1,p(x)/q(x)) and samples from the positive residual after rejection.
claims.notes: Applies to standard rejection sampling, not all proposed optimizations.

claims.claim: Expected accepted prefix length equals sum_{i=1}^K a^i under independent, constant per-position acceptance probability a.
claims.notes: Synthetic iid model; not a prediction of production acceptance or speed.

claims.claim: Speculative decoding is most useful in supported medium-to-low QPS / memory-bound regimes, and can become slower as verification batch costs grow.
